title: Push cachetools mutation kill rate past 75 percent
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 300 mutants in the installed cachetools/__init__.py of cachetools==5.3.3. Author a pytest suite from scratch under work/gc-351/tests/ that kills at least 75 percent: this requires precise behavioral coverage of every cache class -- eviction order under maxsize and getsizeof pressure, currsize accounting, popitem semantics, TTL and TLRU expiry driven by injected timer callables (never wall-clock sleeps), and the decorator helpers. Expect several plan-grade-triage-regrade cycles; survivors must be read as diffs (mutmut show) and answered with tests that pin the exact boundary each mutation moved. Fail-closed grading: red baseline, suite slower than 5 seconds, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift scores kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi cachetools==5.3.3 (target under mutation: Cache, LRUCache, LFUCache, RRCache, TTLCache, TLRUCache)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-351/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-351/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-351/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-351/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-351/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
An honest per-iteration log of wall-clock and LLM spend exists at work/gc-351/cost_log.md, including failed iterations.
